summary: This has ignited some fears within the community of the COD-ification of Battlefield.
body: A few things come to mind when I think about what the greatest fear of a Battlefield player is. It could be a glint atop the mountains on Liberation Peak, reliving the launch of Battlefield 2042 , or maybe it's the randomised recoil from the first Battlefield. All of these are good bets, but I think the real shared nightmare of most Battlefield players is that someday it'll morph into Call of Duty . To be fair, this fear isn't entirely unfounded. Bryan Beede was previously appointed as Battlefield's general manager after spending 19 years working on Call of Duty and has now been promoted to group general manager at EA. Taking his place is another Call of Duty veteran, Sam Cooper, who worked as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service. (Image credit: DICE) "I'm excited to share that I've joined Electronic Arts as general manager of Battlefield," Cooper says in a LinkedIn post . "I started my games career at EA on the FIFA team, so coming back to where it all began feels extra special. summary: Well, there's no accounting for taste.
body: Remember that 007 First Light song Lana Del Rey surprised-dropped earlier this year that I said wasn't very good because, as I put it at the time, "it sounds like Bond karaoke"? body: The Leviathan, the 111-meter superyacht owned by Valve co-founder Gabe Newell, has a number of unconventional features. It has a pool for SCUBA testing. But for the industry experts at Superyacht Times, which recently released a walkthrough video of the Leviathan's features and operating philosophy (via GamesRadar ), the most remarkable thing about Newell's roving wave-palace is its owner's willingness to appreciate the crew that enables his lifestyle of seaborne excess. title: Final Fantasy 14's ongoing pursuit in making its 500-hour story less daunting almost manifested into something in August, but Yoshi-P decided to postpone it
summary: We'll get there… one day.
body: I love Final Fantasy 14. I can also recognise that for anyone trying to start the game in the big 2026, it's incredibly daunting. Being faced with A Realm Reborn and five entire expansions' worth of story is a lot, and the question of how to funnel new players into Eorzea in a more approachable manner while still respecting the MMO's heavily narrative-driven vibe has been an ongoing debate for the last several years. We know, at the very least, that director and producer Naoki Yoshida has been thinking about ways to make that barrier to entry a little less frightening— he said as much during Final Fantasy 14's Berlin Fan Festival —but according to a recent Letter from the Producer , it turns out we could've actually had something as recently as August. "The idea of letting players freely choose a starting point for their adventure has been discussed, with the goal being to offer players a range of choices, rather than prescribe their experience according to my philosophy," Yoshida wrote. title: World of Warcraft: Forever player turns their paladin into a near-unkillable healbot, solos a level 60 monster at level 30, and swims into the ocean
summary: It took 20 minutes, though.
body: World of Warcraft: Forever's having some teething issues with its new spellcaster itemisation. The idea, to sum it up quick, is that a lot of the power that was in spells innately has been pushed onto items, instead, with the intention to make it feel really good when you get a cool new staff as a mage, for instance. This has had unintended consequences, as discovered by Rextroy (the same madlad who solos raid bosses ), as shared on YouTube . The problem is this: Gear in Forever can give a lot of raw power to your healing and damage spells, as part of the aforementioned changes. But that raw power also applies to lower-level healing spells, too. In Forever (and in Classic), casting lower-level spells is a core part of managing your mana as a healer. In this instance, however, "the healing coefficient on healing power remains the same, which is around 43% [on a low level Flash of Light], so if I stack all healing green items, I get my healing power up towards 242," Rextroy explains. title: Intel hit with class action alleging it 'misled investors' – company's recent downturn due in part to how darn expensive PCs are right now
summary: The company saw a large stock price decline just last week.
body: Hot on the heels of a monumental share price drop for the company, Intel now faces a class action lawsuit from its own shareholders. This is according to an alert from law firm Robbins LLP , which recently informed all investors. This suit alleges "Intel misled investors about demand for its products and the Company's future growth potential." The class action can involve anyone who bought stock between July 23, 2026, and October 29, 2026, known as the "class period". With the memory crisis in full effect, PC sales are down worldwide ( estimated to be 20% down in October ), but the lawsuit argues that the PC sales slowdown was "having a materially greater negative impact to Intel’s third quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Group results than defendants had disclosed to investors." It also argues Intel's OEM and distribution partners were left with hardware they couldn't sell to consumers due to rising prices, and that positive impacts of Intel business coming from the AI boom were off "more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup." title: WoW: Forever's continued to wrestle with dungeons, as Blizzard admits it briefly 'missed the mark' on hotfixes over the weekend
summary: Out on the level range.
body: World of Warcraft: Forever 's been pretty great. At this point, I have around 150 hours played, a terrible posture problem, and a level 47 warrior I just barely avoided doing a 2 am Zul'Farrak run with yesterday. Speaking of, there has been a point of contention: Dungeons. My position on the debate is fairly neutral —I think you could maybe bump up the mob XP by around 10% as a compromise—but overall I think they're fine. The new ones are bangers, and I get a huge bunch of XP from doing them at least once. Blizzard's recent choices, however, did have me scratching my head over the weekend. For a short time, via a hotfix , enemies in dungeons wouldn't give experience points to anyone in the group if they were trivial (that is, greyed out) to at least one party member. On paper, this sounds incredibly reasonable. WoW has suffered from a plague of dungeon boosters (that is, people selling runs of dungeons to let folks AFK through their levelling journey) particularly in Classic. But the moment you take a second to stare at how Classic dungeons are designed, you start to see the cracks form. Uldaman, for instance, has a level range of 41-51 in my dungeon finder. title: Influential Warhammer miniature designer Aly Morrison has died
summary: Morrison retired just six months ago.
body: Miniature designer and artist Aly Morrison has died, as confirmed by Trish Carden Miniatures and Design on Facebook . Carden, Morrison's ex-wife and former partner in Marauder Miniatures, posted that, "Mharaid and I are heartbroken to announce the passing of Aly Morrison, a very much loved father, veteran wargames miniatures designer and friend to many around the tabletop and the world. Aly passed unexpectedly but peacefully this Wednesday, and will be sorely missed." Aly Morrison began sculpting for Citadel in 1983 as a freelancer before joining the studio full-time in 1986. He and Trish were then made stewards of Games Workshop's imprint Marauder Miniatures in 1988, where they had free reign to create quirky and characterful figures like the mohawked dwarf trollslayers and the giant with a whaler's beard and a booze barrel strapped to his waist that became archetypal parts of Warhammer. Morrison also crafted the first miniatures for Blood Bowl players and drew the tokens to represent them in the board game's first edition. title: Are you more of an ambient music enjoyer or theatrical atmosphere appreciator?
summary: Quiet and unassuming, or loud and proud?
body: When World of Warcraft: Forever's beta first launched, I lamented its long stretches of silence and penchant for ambience over theatrics. I still sort of stand by that, but after spending more time in Azeroth (and discovering the loop music setting) I've a new-found appreciation for both WoW's soundtrack and ambient music as a whole. It's also got me thinking about what makes a soundtrack ambient versus something more melodic. I'm chronically Final Fantasy 14-brained, where just about everything has a grand thematic soundtrack to it—the jauntiness of the Gold Saucer, the soothing Middle-earthness of Gridania's outer Shroud zones, the grand organs of Ishgard's bitterly cold landscape. You can't escape composer Masayoshi Soken's penchant for leifmotifs. He will turn anything into an orchestral spectacle. I'm a big JRPG fan in general, a genre I think is the absolute master of thematic soundtracks. But I also think fondly of games I've played over the years that are a little more pared down, their soundtracks there for a little atmosphere rather than actively driving the narrative. Minecraft's OST is a masterclass in ambience, and is in regular rotation across my videogame-themed Spo…

title: The pandemic was transformative for Jackbox: 'We went from a gamer name to a household name'
summary: "People realized how easy it was to just share the screen over a Zoom call and everyone's playing."
body: It's no secret that the Covid-19 pandemic saw a lot of people using videogames to stave off lockdown blues, and the Jackbox Party Pack games were especially well-suited for the role: easy-to-understand party fare that's optionally family-friendly and easy to play over a video call. PC Gamer said as much back in March 2020. In a recent interview with PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield, Jackbox Games CEO Mike Bilder said that the pandemic proved transformative for the developer. "The industry at large obviously saw a lot of success at that time, but we did as well, and we went from a gamer name to a household name," he said, noting it was an "unfortunate period of time for the world, but for the gaming industry, a good one, and for Jackbox, a good one as well." "That was kind of a leveling up for Jackbox as a company," said Bilder. "Suddenly office workers are doing happy hours and families over weekends are connecting over a game of Quiplash or something because it's what you did when you were locked down. People realized how easy it was to just share the screen over a Zoom call and everyone's playing." It surprised employees at the studio to see how popular the games had bec…

summary: The filmmaker and author of Terrible Old Games You've Probably Never Heard Of gives us a tour of his Steam library.
body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?" Stuart Ashen—better known by his YouTube persona Ashens—grew up on a diet of 8-bit games on consoles like the Atari 2600 and the Spectrum. The earliest PC game he recalls playing was Syndicate Wars on his first home-built rig—a Pentium 200 MMX machine housed in a server tower case: "I loved Syndicate . Hated Syndicate Wars. Never got on with it at all," he says. "Ended up giving it to a friend who loved it … I think I went on to Duke Nukem 3D or something." A YouTuber since 2006, Ashens is known primarily for his reviews of weird and (typically not) wonderful food products on his main channel , which to date has 1.67 million subscribers. title: Slay the Spire 2 has a new character in testing, and she's really quite busted
summary: I won't miss.
body: Slay the Spire 2 has a new character—notably, a new character in testing —and as the patch notes themselves point out , that testing will very much be needed: "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch." I decided to hop into the beta branch myself and take her for a whirl, and—yeah, those changes'll have to come. The Fool's central mechanic is her bow and arrow—she can fire an arrow/shoot card to deal damage equal to the card's base damage plus her aim. So if a shoot card deals 15 damage and she has six aim stocked, she'll deal 21. This is a little busted, because by default, the Fool has 6 aim already put in her bank. Her non-strike starter card, Foolish Shot, already deals a hefty 15 damage for just one energy. With aim, the first time she uses it, it deals a whopping 21 damage, which is a heck of a damage output for the Fool's first round of combat. The saving grace here is that when a card that fires an arrow is used, that arrow becomes lodged in a target, who gains the Impale status. You can't play any more arrow-based cards until you either Dislodge (another game term, hence the proper nounage) an arrow with…

title: Former survival MMO Dune: Awakening can now be played 'without requiring an Internet connection at any point' as its much requested offline mode arrives
summary: Everything including 'creating and deleting single-player characters' can be done without touching the web.
body: At long last, the transfer of power is complete. Dune: Awakening , Funcom's ambitious survival MMO based on the classic sci-fi novel, has completed is pivot away from massive multiplayer, and can now be played fully offline. The offline function arrived in an otherwise unremarkable patch that mainly fixes specific bugs and technical issues. "It's now possible to play the game in single-player mode without requiring an internet connection at any point, including creating and deleting single-player characters.," Funcom revealed in a Steam post. Dune: Awakening has been gradually drifting away from being a purely multiplayer experience for some time. In April, Funcom made its PvP element, like the Deep Desert and shipwreck exploration, fully optional . A fully fledged single-player mode arrived in September, including a dramatic rework of several major endgame systems—like its dynamic political "Landsraad" system' to make them work in solo play. At that point, single-player still required an Internet connection. Now though, that's no longer the case. To be clear, Dune: Awakening can still be played with all its multiplayer and PvP trappings, now including a "Go Online" button for exa…

title: The most annoying questgivers in PC games
summary: The XP isn't worth it.

That means she puts you in harm's way quite a lot, which many players hate her for. Others just hate her voice. I think her positive outlook makes a refreshing change of pace from, you know, everything else going on in Fallout 3. Plus she gives you an armored Vault suit just for starting her questline, and the Wasteland Survival Guide she writes with your help goes on to be a useful item in both New Vegas and Fallout 4. title: Is the game funny, or just the players? Jackbox CEO says they get 'a lot of false positives' with a staff of comedy writers
summary: Testing comedy games comes with a unique challenge.
body: Social improv games like those in Jackbox 's Party Packs can have vastly different vibes depending on who you're playing with. Meemaw isn't likely to appreciate the phrase "glup shitto" the way your PC gaming friends will, and those sorts of high-variance dynamics are something Jackbox Games has to stay acutely aware of, according to CEO Mike Bilder. "I mean we do a ton [of testing] internally, but then as games get greenlit, we'll bring in external groups," Bilder told PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield in a recent interview. "We want to make sure that we're not just local-biased with our own opinions on things. We want to make sure these games are playing well." Something that makes it especially hard to tell whether a game is funny or they're just having a good session is the fact that they work with comedy writers—people who can make a boring game seem funny just by cracking jokes while they play. "We get a lot of false positives because we have such funny people here that work in the office, and they make games shine," said Bilder. title: Do you like mob tagging in oldschool MMOs, or are you done with fighting for quest credit?
summary: Tag, you're it.
body: Terminally Online (Image credit: Future) This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice. I've been having a pleasant time with WoW: Forever (and by that, I mean it has consumed nearly every waking moment of my life). One thing, however, has been made pretty clear: Mob tagging, that is, only giving kill credit to the first player (or group) to damage a mob, is divisive. One side of the fence—my side, I'm afraid—does see mob tagging as a necessary evil in an MMO that's trying to drive social interaction. Videogames, particularly ones that are incentivising you to group up, are kind of meant to be a pain in the butt sometimes; if you've got a "kill 20" quest and there another person there, the fact you might get in each other's way if you don't group up, and have a jollier time if you do, is a net good. title: Dishonored 2 director Harvey Smith wants to honour sacred imsim texts while finding new ways to surprise fans: 'That's the two wolves inside me'
summary: "On one hand, I want to pay off those expectations. On the other hand, I want to exceed them."
body: Harvey Smith remembers the 10 months he spent as quality assurance lead on System Shock as a "brush with greatness". "I had loved Ultima Underworld, and then I got to work with the very people that were rolling off of Underworld onto this new cyberpunk game," he says. "Looking Glass fought like cats and dogs, but man, they were passionate about what they were doing. And this was a mission for them." (Image credit: Nightdive) Afterwards, when Smith joined System Shock producer Warren Spector at Ion Storm Austin, "we just applied that same hunger to Deus Ex ," he says. "And then when I got together with Raphaël Colantonio, we were like, 'Why just live a normal life? Why fucking punch in and sit at a desk and run some numbers? We're just dying to do this, right?' And so we made Dishonored ." It's a simplified take on the story—one that skips the wilderness years spent fighting for funding before Arkane partnered with Bethesda. title: Yes, some brave games are still launching on Steam during GTA 6 week
summary: Roundabouts, merchant republics, and dark fantasy roguelikes aren't budging their release plans.
body: Though it might seem hard to believe given its inescapability, not everyone is going to be playing GTA 6 next week. Some might be waiting for its eventual PC release (whenever that ends up being). Others might simply be unwilling to spend over a thousand dollars on a console just to enjoy the privilege. Most publishers and developers releasing a videogame this season, however, have opted to vacate the GTA 6 blast radius—but not all of them. If you're looking for something new to play next week, you'll be pleased to know there are some brave games still launching on Steam. Here are some options to consider if you aren't dropping into Vice City: Crusader Kings 3: Silk and Silver (Image credit: Paradox) If you're a CK3 player—and you should be; it's number eight on our Top 100 list for a reason—then Paradox's next expansion should be on your radar. title: A survival game we once called 'Stalker and Tarkov's alien baby' is closing down less than a year after launch
summary: Pioner seemed headed in the right direction when it went into early access in late 2025, but it all went wrong just a few months later.
body: Pioner, a survival-shooter we said looked like " Stalker and Tarkov's alien baby " when we first laid eyes on it in 2021, is ending development and closing down. In an announcement posted today on Steam, developer GFAGames said further work on the game and continued operation of its servers requires more money, and it just doesn't have any. "Over the past few months, we have been in talks with existing and potential partners about investment and new ways of working together that would allow us to preserve the project and the team," the studio wrote. "We were unable to agree on the funding needed to continue the project. The studio no longer has sufficient funds of its own to continue development and keep the servers running." Pioner looked promising when it turned up at the PC Gaming Show in 2021: A mash-up of Stalker, Metro, and Escape From Tarkov that featured both a singleplayer campaign and online co-op and PvP survival action, all of it built around late Soviet-era technology. It launched into early access in December 2025 and worked its way to a peak concurrent player count of 1,686 on Steam a few months later—not huge, but far from catastrophic, and trending in the right di…

title: I cannot stop everyone staring at me in GTA 5

body: Los Santos Customs I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier . As we've covered in previous lectures, everyone is Franklin . This is disconcerting. Even more disconcerting is that, as of today, all the Franklins now have a singular object of cathexis: Franklin. Uh, that is to say, Franklin Prime: me. I have installed Look At Me , a Grand Theft Auto 5 mod whose purpose is to make you the centre of attention wherever you go and wherever you teleport. In the street, crowds round on you, fixing you with a silent stare as though they know everything you've ever done, everything you will ever do. Even parkour does not mollify them. title: 8BitDo Ultimate 3E wireless controller review
summary: Is Xbox wireless connectivity and modularity really worth that price?
body: Pricing has remained the elephant in the room for almost all PC Gaming hardware this year, but when it comes to controllers, you don't even have the memory crisis to blame. And yet, I feel similarly about the 8BitDo Ultimate 3E as I do all that memory-equipped hardware: This is genuinely an excellent gamepad that I have loved reaching for every day, but that price stings so badly that it becomes quite hard to recommend. Unless, of course, you really want a dual-compatible (Xbox and PC) modular wireless controller. Buy if… ✅ You want the best wireless pad for your Xbox: The Ultimate 3E acts exactly like the standard Microsoft Xbox controller, even waking up the console with the on button, except it's better in almost every way. Don't buy if… ❌ You want the best value for money: You can get the GameSir G7 Pro, with its tri-mode connectivity and charging stand for nearly half the price.
